extracted.intended_audience: web developers and site authors using MathJax; accessibility engineers integrating math into web pages
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for making mathematical content rendered by MathJax accessible to users of screen readers, braille displays, and keyboard-only navigation. Covers UI behavior, accessibility extensions, configuration options, and cross-platform compatibility considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: WCAG 2.0 compliance for MathJax menu
rubrics_metrics.description: The MathJax Menu follows WCAG 2.0 guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each expression typeset by MathJax is included in the tab order by default (can be disabled via a menu option). When an expression is focused the menu can be triggered via the space or menu key; navigation in the menu is possible using the arrow keys; a menu selection can be made using the Enter or Return key; and the menu can be closed without making a selection using the Escape or Esc key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default keyboard focusability of expressions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each expression typeset by MathJax is included in the tab order by default.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This behavior can be turned off via a menu option. Focusing an expression should allow keyboard users to open the MathJax contextual menu and explore the expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of WAI-ARIA attributes for assistive technologies
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility extensions use standard web accessibility APIs such as WAI-ARIA attributes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In particular MathJax inserts aria-label and aria-braillelabel attributes (among others) so that screen readers and braille devices can obtain speech and braille representations without relying on native MathML support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsive rendering via collapsing and exploration
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide responsive rendering of mathematical content through collapsing and exploration of subexpressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The explorer allows users to collapse parts of expressions and descend into subexpressions to view them in a more compact or navigable form, improving comprehension on different devices and contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: On-the-fly aural rendering (speech)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an aural rendering tool that gives on-the-fly speech-text for mathematical content and its subexpressions using user-selectable rule sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speech generation is provided by the a11y/speech component and can be configured with different rule sets to match users' expectations and locale; the explorer coordinates speech with navigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tactile (braille) rendering support
rubrics_metrics.description: Enable tactile rendering (Nemeth or Euro Braille) on a connected Braille display.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support for tactile Braille output devices varies across screen readers, operating systems, and browsers. Users of Braille output devices may need to select the 'Combine with Speech' option in the MathJax contextual menu’s Braille submenu (or press 'b' while exploring) to obtain Nemeth or Euro Braille output rather than the speech text on their Braille device. NVDA users on Windows typically need this; JAWS users may be fine with defaults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interactive exploration features
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an exploration tool that allows meaningful interactive investigation of expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploration includes multiple highlighting features, magnification, synchronized aural rendering, and keyboard commands (essential, advanced, and table-navigation keys). See the 'Available explorer keyboard commands' section for command details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semantic enrichment for improved speech and line breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Use semantic analysis to improve the internal representation of expressions for screen reading and line breaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The a11y/semantic-enrich component analyses expressions to make screen reading and line breaking more accurate and accessible across assistive technologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relying solely on hidden MathML for screen readers
rubrics_metrics.description: Hidden MathML (assistive-mml approach) depended on screen readers' MathML support and produced inconsistent experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because MathML support in screen readers varies widely and can break across browser/reader updates (e.g., screen readers may skip math when reading whole pages), MathJax v4 moved to aria-based speech and explorer components to provide more consistent accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of a11y extensions in combined components (v4 default)
rubrics_metrics.description: In MathJax v4, the extensions for generating speech and exploring expressions are included and enabled in all the combined components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means pages using the combined components should be accessible to users with screen or Braille readers automatically; in v3 these features had to be activated manually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Configurability of accessibility features
rubrics_metrics.description: Accessibility features can be configured or included explicitly in custom builds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enable the contextual menu include ui/menu; you can include any a11y extensions explicitly. The a11y/explorer component makes exploration possible and loads a11y/speech automatically. See 'Accessibility Extensions Options' for configuration details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-platform testing and compatibility goal
rubrics_metrics.description: Support the widest selection of browsers, operating systems, and assistive technologies by using well-supported web standards and testing across platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MathJax tests the assistive tools on 13 different browser/os/screen-reader combinations to ensure the user experience is as seamless as possible; explorer was rewritten in v4 to be more compliant with ARIA and more reliable across combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explorer interaction design goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Explorer is designed to provide reliable interactive reading/navigation of expressions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals include: (1) work across major browser/OS/screen-reader combinations; (2) properly read the full expression when reading the whole page or when stepping through by units; (3) automatically enter 'focus mode' when an expression is focused (in screen readers with separate focus/browser modes); (4) allow control over the description of the math (e.g., 'clickable math') via a menu option; (5) voice 'press H for help' when the math is first focused (this prompt can be turned off by preference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Backward-compatibility option: hidden MathML via contextual menu
rubrics_metrics.description: Contextual menu can turn on hidden MathML to mimic v3 behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turning on hidden MathML will turn off the speech and Braille generation used by the explorer component, for users who prefer the older hidden-MathML experience.
